nodes.claim: The perfect body axiom is one measurement timeline fusing sensors, self-report and derived clinical values — not a set of disconnected trackers.
nodes.detail: Sleep, heart data, activity, nutrition, and clinic-derived values are one body described by channels of different noise and cadence; the perfect axiom models them jointly on a person's timeline. The concrete case the seed asked for now exists, from bod-3's evidence: perceived and device-measured sleep dissociate, and each channel carries predictive signal the other lacks — subjective reports track emotional state, objective measures predict cognition and cardiometabolic risk. A subjective-only axiom therefore mislabels mood as sleep; an objective-only axiom silently discards the channel that carries the affect coupling. Only joint modeling of both channels can attribute a night's signal to the right construct, which is fusion changing a conclusion, not just improving precision. And the discrepancy term itself exists only in the joint representation — it is not computable in either channel alone — which is what makes this fusion rather than parallel tracking. Rises to cited when a study directly demonstrating a fusion-vs-single-channel attribution reversal is in hand; the current argument composes bod-3's cited findings rather than citing one directly.

nodes.claim: Continuous streams stay at the body's edge; only bands cross into the combination.
nodes.detail: The raw stream (beat-by-beat HR, minute steps) has maximal re-identification surface and near-zero marginal value for cross-axiom coupling, which operates at the band/summary grain anyway. The perfect system folds at the edge (device), crosses bands, and keeps the stream where the OS already holds it. Mirrors gen-2: minimizing custody is design quality, not compromise.

nodes.claim: Self-report is a sensor with a knowable bias model, not a channel to discard when hardware arrives — and the two channels predict different things, so the perfect axiom routes them, not ranks them.
nodes.detail: The dissociation is real and large: in 1,483 older adults with home polysomnography, multivariable models over PSG, clinical and demographic measures explained only 11–17% of the variance in next-morning subjective sleep quality (Kaplan 2017). And it is structured, channel-specific prediction rather than one channel being noise: in 83 adults over 7-day actigraphy, objective measures predicted executive-function and memory performance in the upper and lower sleep quartiles while subjective reports did not — and subjective reports, not objective measures, were strongly predicted by emotional state (Sci Rep 2024). On the physiological side the weight inverts: in 255 adults with insomnia disorder, objectively short (<6 h) but not subjectively short sleep carried a 3.59× risk of reporting hypertension (Bathgate 2016); the same objective-not-subjective pattern reappears for incident hypertension in the Sleep Heart Health Study (J Clin Sleep Med, 10.5664/jcsm.10570) and incident cardio/cerebrovascular disease (10.5664/jcsm.11046). So the perfect axiom keeps both channels and ROUTES them: the perception channel feeds affect/wellbeing couplings, the measured channel feeds cognition and physiology couplings, and the discrepancy between them is itself a modeled quantity (its magnitude plausibly tracks distress — the sleep-misperception literature supports this, but it is not established by the three sources here). Caveats held honestly: PSG-comparison designs cannot separate perception from retrospective-reporting bias; a multiday study (Sci Rep 2024, 10.1038/s41598-024-56668-0) finds objective quality does predict subjective ratings, suggesting part of Kaplan's null is a single-night artifact; and consumer wearables' staging error (vs PSG) inflates apparent dissociation. Verification depth: sources corroborated against the public search index (titles, PMIDs/DOIs and findings cross-checked across independent queries); full texts were unreachable from this run's container (scholarly hosts egress-blocked), so claims are abstract-level.
sources: Kaplan KA, Hirshman J, Hernandez B, Stefanick ML, Hoffman AR, Redline S, et al. (2017). When a gold standard isn't so golden: Lack of prediction of subjective sleep quality from sleep polysomnography. Biological Psychology 123:37–46. PMID 27889439

nodes.claim: Meals and scans enter the perfect axiom as derived values, not as artifacts.
nodes.detail: A meal photo stream and a DICOM file are storage-and-liability heavy artifacts whose analytical content, at the coupling grain, compresses to a handful of derived values (diet pattern, imaging-derived measures). The perfect axiom ingests the values with provenance and leaves artifact custody to institutions built for it. The door stays open for a future where on-device models derive values from artifacts locally — which would satisfy this node, not contradict it.

nodes.claim: Within-person change is the design-correct grain for body→mind couplings, and where directly compared (sleep) it beats between-person level — but the ordering is unestablished elsewhere, and the grain pays only as far as the state instrument's reliability.
nodes.detail: Now quantitatively grounded, and it answers central's 2026-08-26 portfolio question. The direct within-vs-between comparison exists for sleep→self-control: meta-analytically, within-individual r = .35 [.24, .45] for sleep quality and r = .20 [.09, .31] for duration — both LARGER than the corresponding between-individual estimates (.26 and .14) (Guarana 2021). That is this node's claim measured — with the honest caveat that the within- and between-individual confidence intervals overlap substantially, so the ordering is a consistent point-estimate direction rather than a statistically separated difference. Scope, corrected 2026-08-29 after the adversarial pass: the direct within-vs-between comparison still exists for sleep only. The endocrine and metabolic fronts (bod-9, bod-10) show within-person affect couplings that are small in absolute terms, which bounds the PAYOFF of the grain on those fronts but does not test the ORDERING — no within-vs-between comparison of one same coupling exists there — and bod-10 adds the standing condition that occasions pay only as far as the state instrument's reliability (bod-7). The claim is scoped to the design-grain argument plus the demonstrated sleep ordering, no longer 'most couplings'. The best-evidenced single coupling by volume is prior-night sleep → next-day affect: a meta-analysis of 118 intensive-longitudinal (diary/EMA) studies finds small-to-moderate within-person correlations — better-than-usual subjective sleep quality and longer-than-usual sleep predicting improved next-day affect — with the reverse direction weaker and absent for total sleep time (Bourke 2026). A well-powered single anchor: in 1,982 adults over 8 daily interviews, nights of shorter-than-own-usual sleep predicted blunted positive-affect responses to both stressors and positive events, with no evidence for the reverse direction (Sin 2020). What is NOT the anchor: acute sleep loss → risk-taking, whose direction is unstable across sex, framing and protocol in the recent synthesis literature — central should not hang cen-2 on risk specifically. Caveats: within-person correlations are generally stronger when sleep is self-reported rather than objectively measured (the meta-analysis's own wording — 'generally', not 'consistently', and 'objectively measured', not specifically actigraphy; corrected 2026-08-29 on re-verification), so part of the coupling is appraisal rather than physiology — which is not a defeater here, because bod-3's channel routing makes the perception channel a legitimate sensor; and the experimental (causal) leg is mostly acute total deprivation rather than naturalistic night-to-night variation. Verification depth as bod-3: search-index corroborated, abstract-level, full texts egress-blocked this run.

nodes.claim: Trait↔body cross-connections run through regulatory-system parameters — autonomic, immune, endocrine, metabolic — not through anatomy, and their honest between-person effect sizes are small.
nodes.detail: The owner's cross-connection question (2026-08-25), first half of the answer. The couplings that replicate between traits the other axioms measure and the body are all regulatory parameters, not anatomical features. Autonomic: heart rate variability (indices pooled across computation methods) ↔ top-down self-regulation (executive function, emotion regulation, effortful control) across 123 studies, N=14,347 — significant and SMALL, r ≈ .09 (Holzman & Bridgett 2017); the sibling meta-analysis on HRV↔self-control finds a small effect with significant publication bias that goes non-significant after bias adjustment (Zahn 2016) — so r ≈ .09 is an upper bound, not a point estimate. Immune: higher conscientiousness → lower C-reactive protein across three national samples (N=26,305) plus meta-analysis (N=34,067), lowest-conscientiousness quartile carrying up to 50% higher risk of clinically elevated CRP (≥3 mg/L); openness weakly negative; neuroticism, extraversion, agreeableness null (Luchetti 2014). Depression↔inflammation shows moderate case-control elevations of CRP and IL-6 with REDUCED variability in patients for CRP — a right-shift of the whole distribution rather than an inflamed subgroup, which is exactly how a continuous regulatory parameter, not a discrete lesion, behaves (Osimo 2020). Two consequences for the perfect axiom. First, the cross-connection layer is a STATE-PARAMETER INTERFACE — a small vector of regulatory set-points and reactivities per person-period — not a body map. Anatomical couplings are not absent but are weaker in matched currency: ENIGMA-MDD finds hippocampal volume reduction in depression at Cohen's d = -0.14 (1,728 patients vs 7,199 controls; d = -0.17 for recurrent MDD) against Osimo's CRP elevation at g = 0.71 in the same case-control currency — a roughly fivefold gap — and a systematic review and meta-analysis of Big Five traits against structural MRI ('Nothing to see here', Personality Neuroscience) finds no reliable trait-level structural differences at all. Anatomy is the substrate; the regulatory parameters carry the signal. Second, effect-size currency is part of the connection: case-control group differences (moderate) and trait-level per-SD correlations (small) are different quantities, and publishing one as the other would overstate the axis severalfold — every published coupling declares its currency. Because the between-person couplings are this small, the cross-axis power that remains lives within-person, which is why this node depends on bod-5. Mirrors gen-9: architecture, not gene lists; systems, not organs. Verification depth as bod-3.

nodes.claim: A trait–body channel exists only as far as its body-side instrument's construct validity — where the instrument collapses, the perfect axiom declares the channel unmeasured rather than small.
nodes.detail: The owner's cross-connection question, second half — the boundary. Cardiac interoception is the cautionary case: the field's founding instrument, the heartbeat counting task, produces scores contaminated by time-estimation ability and prior beliefs about one's own heart rate, with systematic undercounting driving 'accuracy' (Zamariola 2018; Desmedt and colleagues' follow-ups conclude the scores are largely a reflection of subjective beliefs about heart rate); the critique is itself contested in a published comment-and-response exchange (Zimprich, Nusser & Pollatos 2020; a second commentary by Ainley et al. 2020 and a reply from the original authors, PMID 32061686, complete the exchange), so the demolition is not settled either — but a 133-study meta-analysis (N=11,524) from the same Louvain research group as the original critique (independence duly noted) finds heartbeat-counting performance carries little relation to the mental-health outcomes the theory predicted (null for trait anxiety, depression and alexithymia), and a separate meta-analysis finds the two putative measures of the same construct — counting vs discrimination accuracy — share only a small (if significant) relation (Hickman et al. 2020). When that happens, 'interoceptive accuracy ↔ emotion' is not a small coupling — it is an unmeasured channel, because the body-side number is not measuring the channel. The general law the perfect axiom takes from this: instrument reliability mechanically caps every observable trait–body correlation (attenuation), so bod-6's 'small' is partly an artifact ceiling, and the honest cross-connection publishes each channel's instrument reliability and validity status WITH its couplings — three states: measured (validated instrument), attenuated (valid but noisy, correctable), unmeasured (construct validity failed). This is the body-side twin of que-2's claim that a question is an instrument with estimable parameters. Verification depth as bod-3.

nodes.claim: An observed trait–body coupling does not fix its direction or mechanism, and current design-based decomposition (Mendelian randomization, statistical mediation) is itself marker- and design-sensitive — so the perfect cross-connection publishes each coupling's decomposition status, unknowns and unsearched limbs declared.
nodes.detail: Risen argued→cited 2026-08-29 on re-verified sources; the corrections forced along the way are themselves the lesson. The showcase is inflammation↔depression under Mendelian randomization: CRP–symptom coheritability largely reassigns to metabolic dysregulation — BMI potentially causal for anhedonia, tiredness, appetite change and feelings of inadequacy — leaving genetically upregulated IL-6 signaling associated with suicidality only (Kappelmann 2021, GWAS summary data including UK Biobank); in one cohort two markers of the same pathway carry OPPOSITE MR signs — genetically higher IL-6 activity predicting more depressive symptoms, genetically higher CRP fewer (Ye 2021, N up to 144,890); and the sign does not survive cohorts — one-sample MR in HUNT (N=68,769) finds no major causal role for serum CRP, its weakly positive point estimates crossing the null and its conclusion explicitly rejecting Ye's protective direction (Bekkevold 2023), while Lifelines points CRP–anxiety the other way again (Slaney 2025). A 52-article systematic review reports substantial heterogeneity and methodological flaws across depression MR (Ma 2023). So the decomposition instruments disagree among themselves: 'not reliably separated even by design' is the honest current state, and what remains publishable is decomposition STATUS — which components a design has excluded, and how stable that verdict has proven. IL-6 is the best-supported single marker; the one proof-of-concept RCT's effects were still not statistically significant (Foley 2026, JAMA Psychiatry, N=30 — held as a lead). The behavior-mediation limb, corrected: conscientiousness–CRP is virtually unchanged by smoking adjustment and attenuated but not eliminated by BMI (Luchetti 2014) — partial adiposity mediation, not wholesale behavior mediation; and the mediation study last run led with (PMID 29796267) mediates the MPQ achievement facet via physical activity, not conscientiousness, with overlapping measurement windows (Graham 2018) — statistical mediation without temporal ordering, illustrating the problem rather than discharging it. The reverse limb for conscientiousness↔CRP was NOT searched to completion this run — a disease→personality-change pooled analysis (Jokela et al., Psychological Medicine — lead) shows the direction is live — so its status is UNSEARCHED, declared as such; the discipline is declaring unknowns, never assuming them absent. Quantifier softened from the 2026-08-27 form: couplings are decomposable and underdetermined by the observed association — not every component nonzero everywhere. Verification depth as bod-3 (search-index corroborated, abstract-level; scholarly full texts egress-blocked).

nodes.claim: On the endocrine front trait–cortisol couplings are near-null between persons, the momentary affect–cortisol coupling is attenuated-small with no within-vs-between comparison in existence, and most cortisol person-parameters sit at bod-7's attenuated or unmeasured states.
nodes.detail: The endocrine front of the owner's cross-connection question, scouted 2026-08-29. Between persons: the depression–HPA case-control coupling pools to d=0.60 for cortisol (the 671 effect sizes across 361 studies, N=18,454, span cortisol, ACTH and CRH; ACTH d=0.28, CRH null — Stetler & Miller 2011), but the estimate is strongly sample-dependent — outpatient-only d=0.32 vs all-inpatient d=0.74; a 'methods-quality halving to d=0.33' figure failed re-corroboration in the adversarial pass and is not used — and reactivity direction is sex-dependent: currently depressed women blunted, men increased (Zorn 2017, direction only; effect sizes not index-retrievable). Trait–cortisol is near-null: no dedicated personality–cortisol meta-analysis exists (searched this run, none found); up to twelve 24-h urinary measurements over 30 years yield a modest conscientiousness association and no neuroticism relation (Sutin 2022); a Mendelian-randomization lead (SERPINA6/SERPINA1 instruments, PMID 38525495 — single-retrieval) supports morning cortisol→anxiety but not depression or neuroticism. This BOUNDS bod-6's positive half rather than confirming it: not every regulatory parameter carries trait signal — cortisol, the paradigm regulatory parameter, largely does not between persons. Its psychosocial couplings carry p-curve evidential value yet explain only 1–3.6% of awakening-response variance, depression toward higher output and PTSD lower (Boggero 2017 — psychosocial functioning, not personality traits). Within persons, momentary negative affect–cortisol is r=.06 across 38,418 observations, positive affect r=−.05 (Joseph 2021); under bod-7's states this is ATTENUATED, not small-and-final — single momentary saliva samples of a pulsatile analyte with a secretory lag are a weak state instrument, so r=.06 is a lower bound — and no within-vs-between comparison of one same coupling exists on this front, so bod-5's ordering is untested here, not refuted. What is firm is instrument-side: cortisol-awakening-response day-to-day reliability is too poor for individual-differences research while total-output AUCg is fair-to-good (ICCs 0.00–0.75 — Norton 2023); a stable diurnal slope needs ~10 sampling days (Segerstrom 2014); the consensus guidelines demand objective awakening-time verification most studies still lack (Stalder 2016; the 2022 update found little improvement); and hair cortisol runs +22% with stressor exposure, +43% ongoing, yet shows no consistent association with questionnaire-measured perceived stress (Stalder 2017, N=10,289) — read with its months-scale grain and its non-stress determinants (age, sex, hair-washing, BMI) in view. Net: most cortisol channels sit at 'attenuated', single-timepoint cortisol at 'unmeasured' as a person parameter. Verification depth as bod-3, with per-figure flags above where retrieval was single or failed.

nodes.claim: On the metabolic front between-person trait couplings are small and partly adiposity-routed, HbA1c is an excellent person parameter while per-meal glucose responses fail test–retest even under controlled feeding, and within-person glucose–affect coupling is weak and percept-dominated — the measured channel's live within-person coupling is cognition under diabetic-scale excursions.
nodes.detail: The metabolic front, scouted 2026-08-29. Between persons bod-6 holds: conscientiousness is the only Big Five trait coupled to incident diabetes — OR 0.87 (0.82–0.91) per SD, attenuated by obesity adjustment (the attenuation fraction failed re-corroboration; held below citation) (Jokela 2014, pooled N=34,913; obesity itself OR 0.84 per SD — Jokela 2013, n=78,931); depression→incident type 2 diabetes is RR 1.60 in the 2008 meta (Mezuk 2008) and 1.18 (1.12–1.24) in the modern 21-study meta (Graham 2020). Two findings are new to the theory. First, the instrument currencies must be kept apart (bod-6's own rule): HbA1c is a superb trait-grain instrument — within-subject CV ≈1.7% in healthy adults (PLOS ONE 2023 meta) — while the state grain splits in two. True test–retest reliability of the glucose response is poor even under metabolic-ward duplicate meals (ICC 0.31 Abbott / 0.14 Dexcom, 1,189 responses, N=30 — AJCN 2025), so a per-meal response is not a stable personal parameter; but free-living day-to-day profile reproducibility of ICC 0.30 in normoglycemic adults (Matabuena 2023, N=581) mixes real behavioral state variance with noise — not by itself instrument unreliability; real within-person variance is what within-person designs feed on. No study found this run quantifies the CGM days needed for stable nondiabetic estimates, and bod-5's grain pays only as far as the state instrument's reliability (bod-7). Second, where within-person affect coupling exists it runs through the PERCEPT: the only systematic review of glucose-variability–mood finds no clear empirical support (4 of 8 studies positive — Muijs 2021); a 15-adolescent CGM-EMA pilot reports couplings it itself calls small (Zink 2020; numeric figures a single-retrieval lead); perceived glucose variability and perceived hyperglycemia dominate daily diabetes distress — a disease-specific appraisal outcome, not affect proper — while CGM-measured variability is non-significant (Ehrmann 2024, N=379, 17 days); and in healthy adults metabolic-state ratings mediate glucose→mood (eBioMedicine 2025, N=90, four weeks). The measured channel's live within-person coupling is cognitive, at excursions only diabetes produces: low and high glucose slow processing speed within five minutes in type 1 diabetes, sustained attention null, and slight above-mean elevations run FASTER — non-monotonic (GluCog 2024, N=200); a nondiabetic null (CGM metrics vs cognition, PMID 39261457) is methods-only at abstract level and held uncorroborated. The between-person glycemia–dementia gradient is small (HR 1.18, 1.04–1.33, 115-vs-100 mg/dL nondiabetic — Crane 2013) and MR of HbA1c on reaction time is null (Garfield 2021 — lead): even the gradient may be non-causal. Verification depth as bod-3, with per-figure flags above.

nodes.claim: bod-3's channel routing — affect coupling to the perception channel, cognition to the measured channel — recurs on the metabolic front; whether it is a general law is open, with common-method variance the rival explanation a decisive design must break.
nodes.detail: Composition of cited findings (bod-1's precedent), scoped by this run's adversarial pass. The pattern: sleep — subjective reports track emotional state while objective measures predict cognition and cardiometabolic risk (bod-3), and within-person sleep–affect correlations are generally stronger for self-reported than objectively measured sleep (Bourke 2026, in bod-5's sources); metabolic — metabolic-state ratings mediate glucose→mood and perceived variability dominates diabetes distress while CGM-measured variability is non-significant, yet measured glucose moves processing speed (bod-10). Construct honesty about those legs: diabetes distress is a disease-specific appraisal, not affect proper — of the perception-side outcomes only eBioMedicine's mood measure is genuinely affect. The endocrine front contributes an ADJACENT dissociation, not an instance: hair cortisol tracks objective stressor exposure but not perceived stress (bod-9) — a measured-channel/perception-variable dissociation with no affect outcome, which the pattern does not yet cover. The rival explanation, named: every perception→affect leg so far is same-instrument, same-moment self-report (diary→diary, app→app, EMA→EMA) while every measured leg is cross-method — common-method variance predicts exactly this pattern with no routing law at all (bod-3 carries the sleep version of this caveat; it applies with full force here). What survives either way: the perception channel is a different sensor with a different referent, not a degraded copy of the measured channel, and on current evidence it is the affect-relevant one — so every published cross-connection declares its channel (perceived vs measured) as part of bod-7's instrument status, and a coupling computed on one channel is never quoted for the other; a body axiom that waits for hardware measures the wrong channel for an important class of its couplings. Rises to cited only on a design that breaks the method confound — perception and measured channels predicting an affect outcome assessed by a third method within one study; eBioMedicine 2025's mediation shape (in bod-10's sources) is closest but still same-method on the affect side.
